description.en: Dominican salves combine call-and-response singing with religious traditions. Their roots bring together African and Hispanic elements, with some versions sung a cappella and others using tambourines, güiras and drums, notably in Villa Mella.

description.en: Dominican dembow is an urban music form built around a strongly repeated rhythm. The Dominican adaptation speeds up and simplifies the dembow pattern, with artists such as El Alfa and Chimbala belonging to a scene distinct from merengue and bachata traditions.

description.en: Son heard in the Dominican Republic belongs to a musical tradition born in eastern Cuba. This singing and dance genre combines Hispanic and African features, including the tres and call-and-response structures, helping explain musical exchanges across the Caribbean.

description.es: El acordeón produce su sonido al mover un fuelle que impulsa aire sobre lengüetas. Sus teclas o botones permiten interpretar melodía y acompañamiento; en República Dominicana ocupa un lugar reconocido en el merengue, dentro de la difusión internacional del instrumento.
description.en: The accordion produces sound through bellows that move air across reeds. Its keys or buttons allow melody and accompaniment to be played together, and in the Dominican Republic it has a recognized role in merengue within the instrument’s worldwide spread.

description.en: Bolero is a romantic song genre that originated in eastern Cuba in the late nineteenth century. It emerged from the trova tradition and spread through Latin America through solo singers and guitar ensembles, forming a Caribbean background for recognizing its musical language.
